newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-PORTUGAL'S NELSON BLASTS FOREIGN MOANERS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PORTUGAL'S NELSON BLASTS FOREIGN MOANERS.

text.p: Aston Villa's Portuguese full-back Fernando Nelson has hit out at the foreign players complaining at being unable to adjust to English football and the way of life in this country.

Nelson, who joined premier league Villa from Sporting Lisbon in the last off-season, claimed the current problems highlighted by Brazilian Emerson's differences with Middlesbrough could have been avoided had players made the effort to become better prepared before moving to England.
Emerson has left Middlesbrough three times in the last month, saying his wife Andrea was homesick and ill in the northeast of England.
Juninho, another Brazilian at Middlesbrough, Frenchman David Ginola at Newcastle and West Ham's Romanian Florin Raducioiu have complained at times about the physical nature of the English game.

Nelson, who has won five Portugal caps, said: "It's not just a case of looking at the club and what they do. Players should look at the city they will be based in and the way of life. That's what I did. I went into things thoroughly before agreeing to sign for Villa.
"The important thing was that when Villa came in for me I was prepared for what to expect over here and the type of game played, although you need time to adjust.

"But if players come over here and find they do not like the way football is played, it is wrong to complain. I am trying to adapt to the English way and believe I am improving, but it is important foreign players adapt to their club -- not the other way round."
